name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Use a 6px solid focus ring at 7:1 contrast with no glow or animation. This meets WCAG 2.2 AA for keyboard users while keeping the ring visible on all backgrounds. The thicker ring improves touch accuracy on mobile without relying on color alone. Trade-off: it takes slightly more space, but that’s better than risking users missing the focus indicator.

name: Reader
text: A 6px ring at 7:1 contrast still risks disappearing on patterned or dark backgrounds—WCAG warns against relying on color alone. A 4px ring at 5:1 contrast with a subtle 1px outer glow (reduced-motion safe) keeps visibility without the space cost. Test both on high-contrast and dark mode; if the glow passes, it’s the safer choice.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a 4px solid focus ring at 5:1 contrast with a 1px outer glow that’s motion-reduced. This keeps the ring visible on patterned and dark backgrounds without the space cost of a 6px ring. The glow adds no animation and meets reduced-motion needs while improving visibility where color alone fails. Trade-off: the glow is a slight visual cue, but it’s motion-safe and won’t distract users with vestibular sensitivities.

name: Reader
text: The 1px glow at 5:1 contrast risks blending into busy backgrounds just like the 6px ring at 7:1—WCAG warns against any decorative effect that depends on color alone. A 2px dashed ring at 4.5:1 contrast with no glow meets WCAG 2.2 AA, survives dark mode and high-contrast mode, and keeps touch targets large enough. Test it on a zebra-striped table and a dark patterned card; if the dashes stay visible, it’s the safer choice.
